result:
I'm treating this as a new project, staged through New-Project Entry: the package is still a scaffold with only `main()` and smoke tests, and no outcome works on real data. There is no spec. `specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md` is your research brief, and the three research files are background. Each outcome below is a candidate from your brief, for you to confirm, change or drop. I have not ranked them.

## Candidate outcomes

| # | Outcome | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|
| O1 | A real-time vintage panel of CES employment: total nonfarm and supersectors, SA and NSA, by release vintage (1st, 2nd and 3rd print, preliminary and final benchmark). From ces-revisions-prompt.md. | Data volume is small: monthly series, ~15 series × a few hundred vintages. Access is the material cost. The FRED/ALFRED API allows 120 requests/min and needs your API key. NSA vintage coverage is **unknown until checked** and may need archived Employment Situation releases. |
| O2 | Revision scale by each of the four revision stages over time, total and by supersector, with the May 2003 break and 2020–22 marked. From the prompt (Part A). | Cheap once O1 exists. |
| O3 | A split of SA one- and two-month revisions into an NSA-sample part and a seasonal-factor part. From the prompt (Seasonality, Part C). | Depends on NSA vintage coverage (O1). Measured by running it. |
| O4 | The effect of collection interval and first-closing rate on the scale of one-month revisions. From the prompt (Collection interval). | Collection days are arithmetic from release calendars. BLS publishes collection rates by closing, but how far back they go is unknown until fetched. |
| O5 | News vs noise across all four stages, with the benchmark as an irregular higher-precision observation and wedge-back across intervening months. From the prompt (Part C). | Compute can't be estimated without running a fit. |
| O6 | Hand-built yearly capacity covariates: real BLS appropriations, CR, sequestration and shutdown flags, FTE staffing, and CES sample size. Plus whatever association with revision scale can honestly be identified. From the prompt (Funding, Staffing, Sample). | Mostly your time: ~40 fiscal years × ~4 series from budget justifications and FedScope. Archive availability before ~2000 is uncertain. |
| O7 | One joint hierarchical model: covariates in the log-scale, stochastic volatility, Student-t errors, supersector pooling, horseshoe shrinkage. It is compared against a constant-variance baseline (LOO, pseudo-real-time), with a written statement of what is and isn't identified. From the prompt (Part C). | NUTS cost over ~11 supersectors × ~500 months can't be estimated without running it. Analytic marginalization of the state is the main lever. |

Qualities to place when the roadmap is written: manifests, traceability, full validation suites.

## Proposed tracks

- **A: Vintage data and descriptive scale** (O1, O2). Known progression. Every other track needs O1's panel. That is a dependency, not a reason to merge the tracks.
- **B: Seasonal vs sample** (O3). Research. Split off because the decomposition stands without any driver answer.
- **C: Collection interval** (O4). Research. Split off because this is high-frequency, within-year identification and stands without the capacity question.
- **D: Benchmark and news/noise** (O5). Research. Split off because stages 3–4 have different causes (benchmark realignment, birth-death) from the sample-based stages.
- **E: Capacity drivers** (O6). Research. Split off because this is slow, collinear and weakly identified. Joining it to C would make C's answer wait on hand-built covariates.
- **F: Joint model** (O7). Research. It is the synthesis your Part C asks for, and it draws on B–E's machinery.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14 with uv, per `.python-version` and `uv.lock`. Whether JAX and NumPyro have wheels for 3.14 is not yet verified; a quick check is worth doing.
- NumPyro (NUTS), Dynamax, Blackjax only if a custom kernel is needed, ArviZ and Polars, per your brief.

**Proposed roadmap name:** `ces-revisions`, written to `specs/ces-revisions-roadmap.md`. No file by that name exists.

**Optional probe:** if you agree and supply your FRED API key, I can fetch the ALFRED vintage-date list for total nonfarm (PAYEMS) and its NSA counterpart. That would firm up O1's coverage note.

**Your call:** please rank the outcomes within each track, rank the tracks among themselves, and confirm or change the tracks, their kinds and the name.
